questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay based on the chart below. You should start your essay with a brief description of the chart and comment on China's achievements in higher education . You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
The line chart illustrates the changes in the gross enrolment ratio in higher education in China from 1990 to 2019. As is clearly shown, the figure witnessed a steady and remarkable upward trend over these three decades. In 1990, only 3.4% of the eligible population entered higher education. This proportion climbed steadily, passing 11% in 2000 and 30% in 2012, before finally reaching 51.6% in 2019, roughly fifteen times the initial level.

Behind these figures lie China's impressive achievements in higher education. First, the dramatic rise reflects the massive expansion of university enrolment, which has opened the door of college to millions of ordinary families. Moreover, the higher enrolment ratio means a far larger pool of skilled talent, supplying the economy with engineers, doctors and researchers. In my view, such progress not only improves individual prospects but also strengthens the nation's competitiveness.

In conclusion, the steady climb of the enrolment ratio speaks volumes about how far Chinese higher education has advanced, and I firmly believe this positive momentum will continue in the years ahead.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: M: How are you enjoying your new job?
transcript.zh: M: 你觉得新工作怎么样？

transcript.text: W: So far, so good, I don't miss having managers who deliver blunt, harsh feedback in the name of efficiency.
transcript.zh: W: 到目前为止，一切都不错。我一点也不怀念那些以效率为名，给出直白而严厉反馈的经理。

transcript.text: M: From the way you described your last company, no wonder they had a problem with high staff turnover.
transcript.zh: M: 从你描述上一家公司的情况来看，难怪他们会有员工流动率高的问题。

transcript.text: W: Yeah. I couldn't wait to get out of there once my contract expired. The problem with a company culture that prizes directness above all else is that it creates a toxic culture of brilliant jerks that drives people out and erodes itself from within.
transcript.zh: W: 是啊。合同一到期，我就迫不及待地离开了那里。一种把直率看得高于一切的公司文化，问题在于它会造就一种充满才华却为人刻薄的有毒文化，把员工赶走，并从内部逐渐瓦解自身。

transcript.text: M: My company's managers tend to be accommodating and kind, overlooking mistakes or issues so as not to hurt feelings. Issues often get ignored there until they build up and reach a crisis point.
transcript.zh: M: 我们公司的经理往往比较体谅人，也很友善，为了不伤害员工的感情，他们会忽略错误或问题。那里的问题经常一直被忽视，直到越积越多，最终演变成危机。

transcript.text: W: That's not surprising. My new company seems to employ a feedback policy that combines compassion and directness. Employees have the power to speak up, give feedback, disagree and discuss problems in real time. It seems to help us to course correct, improve and meet challenges while also building teams that collaborate and care for one another.
transcript.zh: W: 这并不奇怪。我现在的公司似乎采用了一套兼顾同理心和直率的反馈政策。员工有权表达自己的看法、提出反馈、表示不同意见，并实时讨论问题。这似乎有助于我们及时调整方向、不断改进、应对挑战，同时也能建立起彼此协作、互相关心的团队。

transcript.text: M: But that would be based on an atmosphere of mutual trust, wouldn't it? Otherwise, people might interpret feedback as some kind of personal attack.
transcript.zh: M: 但这应该建立在相互信任的氛围之上，对吧？否则，人们可能会把反馈理解成某种人身攻击。

transcript.text: W: True. Without an atmosphere of trust, feedback can create stress and self-doubt. But I think when we get feedback from someone we trust, we understand that the feedback isn't some kind of personal attack. It's actually a kind of support because it's offered in the spirit of helping us improve. I think sometimes people need to shift their mindsets around how they receive feedback.
transcript.zh: W: 没错。没有信任的氛围，反馈可能会带来压力和自我怀疑。但我认为，当我们从信任的人那里得到反馈时，我们会明白这并不是什么人身攻击。实际上，这是一种支持，因为对方是本着帮助我们进步的态度提出反馈的。我觉得，有时候人们需要改变自己接受反馈的心态。

transcript.text: M: Yes. Constructive feedback, after all, is how we learn and grow. It's the basis for healthy parenting, lasting friendships, career development, and so much more. If we shelter our children, friends, and colleagues from information that might enrich and enhance their lives, we're not being caring. We're actually doing harm to them.
transcript.zh: M: 是的。毕竟，建设性的反馈正是我们学习和成长的方式。它是健康亲子关系、长久友谊、职业发展的基础，作用远不止这些。如果我们不让孩子、朋友和同事接触那些可能丰富并改善他们生活的信息，那就不是在关心他们。实际上，我们是在伤害他们。

transcript.text: W: That's exactly right.
transcript.zh: W: 完全正确。

questions.stem: How does the woman describe her previous company's culture?
questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P4）：The problem with a company culture that prizes directness above all else is that it creates a toxic culture of brilliant jerks that drives people out and erodes itself from within.信号：被问者亲口的定性词 。女士在谈她前公司时，自己直接说出 it creates a toxic culture，“toxic”就是她对那种文化的定性，是被问一方的直接评价，正是答案句的信号。

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音确实念了 in the name of efficiency，efficient 听着耳熟极易勾选；但那是说前公司“打着效率的旗号”给苛刻反馈，是手段不是女士对文化的评价，属典型原词陷阱。 借用原文：accommodating and kind
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：Tolerant（宽容）更接近男士公司“accommodating and kind”那种“迁就”的描述，张冠李戴到女士的前公司头上了；女士前公司的特点是“直接”，不是宽容。
optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：Weird（古怪）在录音里没有任何对应，女士对前公司的评价是“toxic”而非“古怪”，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（it creates a toxic culture ↔ Toxic. 原句形容词直接成选项）

questions.evidenceText: The problem with a company culture that prizes directness above all else is that it creates a toxic culture of brilliant jerks that drives people out and erodes itself from within.

questions.stem: What does the man say about his company's managers?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：My company's managers tend to be accommodating and kind, overlooking mistakes or issues so as not to hurt feelings.信号：男士直接陈述自家管理者 。男士主语直接是 My company's managers tend to be accommodating，紧扣题问的“他公司的管理者”，是说话人对该对象的直接陈述句，定位明确。

optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：ignorant（无知）与录音里多次出现的 "overlooking/ignored”（忽略）读音、含义都沾边，听到 overlooking mistakes 极易误推成“无知”；但男士说的是管理者“故意忽略问题”，不是“无知”，是音/义双重误导。 借用原文：accommodating and kind
optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：Arrogant（傲慢）与男士说的“accommodating and kind”（随和和善）完全相反，男士对自家管理者并无负面评价，选它等于把意思听反了。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：Ambitious（有野心/有抱负）在男士谈管理者的话里没有任何对应，男士说的是“随和、怕伤感情”，与“野心”无关，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（accommodating and kind ↔ They are accommodating. 原文形容词直接入选项）

questions.evidenceText: My company's managers tend to be accommodating and kind, overlooking mistakes or issues so as not to hurt feelings.

questions.stem: What does the woman say the employees in her new company can do?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：Employees have the power to speak up, give feedback, disagree and discuss problems in real time.信号：授权表达 have the power to 。Employees have the power to speak up 用“have the power to”明确点出员工“有权做某事”，正是“can do”题要找…

optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：flexible hours（弹性工时）听着像职场福利、很诱人，但录音通篇讲的是“反馈/发声”，从没提工作时间，属凭印象脑补的无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：break conventions（打破常规）比原文的“disagree/speak up”拔得过高，员工只是“能表异议、讨论问题”，并没有说他们“打破常规”，是过度推断。
optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：think big（有大格局/想大事）原文没有对应，员工被赋予的是“发声、给反馈”的权利，与“想得大”无关，属无中生有兼拔高。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（speak up, give feedback, disagree ↔ They can air their views. 概括同义改写）

questions.evidenceText: Employees have the power to speak up, give feedback, disagree and discuss problems in real time.

questions.stem: What does the man say about constructive feedback?

options.text: It can lead to new discoveries.
It enables people to learn and grow.
It is conducive to critical thinking.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P9）：Constructive feedback, after all, is how we learn and grow.信号：结论口吻 after all + is how we 。Constructive feedback, after all, is how we learn and grow 用 after all 引出总结、is h…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：录音里 mindset 确实被念到——但那是女士说的 people need to shift their mindsets（人要转变接受反馈的心态），不是男士说“反馈能改变心态”；既不是男士说的，作用对象也不同，属张冠李戴式原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：critical thinking（批判性思维）原文从未出现，男士说的是“学习与成长”，硬扯到“批判性思维”是无中生有兼概念拔高。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：new discoveries（新发现）录音里没有任何对应，男士谈的是反馈对“育儿、友谊、职业发展”的益处，与“新发现”无关，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（is how we learn and grow ↔ It enables people to learn and grow. 句式转换同义）

questions.evidenceText: Constructive feedback, after all, is how we learn and grow.

transcript.text: W: How was your holiday? Not too many other tourists around, were there?
transcript.zh: W: 你的假期过得怎么样？周围没太多其他游客吧？

transcript.text: M: No, very few relatively. But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another, trying to find the perfect place. It made me realize that indecision is a big problem for me. Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot.
transcript.zh: M: 没有，相对来说非常少。但我发现自己一直从一个住处搬到另一个住处，试图找到最完美的地方。这让我意识到，优柔寡断对我来说是个大问题。我没有放松下来，反而一直在寻找最好的地方。

transcript.text: W: It seems you suffer from "Fear of Better Options." I've read about it. It describes this loop of indecision as part of our programming. Essentially, we have this tendency to keep stretching out the decision-making process, because as human beings, we are hard-wired to optimize. We have always looked to get the best things we can as a sort of survival of the fittest. Optimizing isn't the problem, but rather the process that we go through.
transcript.zh: W: 看来你患有“更好选择恐惧症”。我读过相关的内容。它把这种优柔寡断的循环描述为我们思维机制的一部分。从本质上说，我们总是倾向于不断延长决策过程，因为作为人类，我们天生就会追求最优选择。一直以来，我们都在努力获得能得到的最好东西，这可以说是一种适者生存。追求最优并不是问题，问题在于我们所经历的过程。

transcript.text: M: Well, that makes me feel better. But I think thanks to technology, we can make comparisons more easily and have more access to choice and customization. We can now see what we could have, how we might get it, and what others have that we might want. We keep looking over and return to the same options again and again.
transcript.zh: M: 嗯，这让我感觉好受多了。但我觉得多亏了科技，我们可以更容易地进行比较，也能有更多选择和定制的机会。现在我们可以看到自己可能拥有什么、可能如何得到它，以及别人拥有而我们可能想要的东西。我们不断回头查看，又一次次回到相同的选项上。

transcript.text: W: Yes. "Fear of Better Options" offers little benefit. It's an ailment of abundance. You must have choices to have that fear of missing out on better options.
transcript.zh: W: 是的。“更好选择恐惧症”几乎没有什么好处。这是过度丰富带来的问题。你必须拥有选择，才会害怕错过更好的选项。

transcript.text: M: Yes, I need to note when I'm worrying about inconsequential things, I guess. If I'm spending too much time worrying over what to have for lunch, I'm robbing myself of the energy to focus on the things that matter.
transcript.zh: M: 是的，我想我需要留意自己什么时候在为无关紧要的事情操心。如果我花太多时间纠结午饭吃什么，就等于消耗了自己的精力，没法专注于真正重要的事情。

transcript.text: W: Exactly. But for more important matters, I think gut instinct might be overrated. When you have 30 odd options, trusting your gut is not practical. What you need to do is research: have a process, invest time exploring your options, and eliminate as many things as you can. The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again.
transcript.zh: W: 没错。不过对于更重要的事情，我觉得凭直觉行事可能被高估了。当你有三十来个选项时，相信直觉并不实际。你需要做的是进行调查研究：建立一个流程，投入时间去了解各种选择，并尽可能排除更多选项。决策过程中最有害的部分，就是一遍又一遍地重复考虑相同的选项。

questions.stem: What does the man say about his holiday?

options.text: He kept looking for the best place to stay.
He met many tourists from other countries.
He had a great time sightseeing and relaxing.
He managed to visit a different city each day.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another, trying to find the perfect place. Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot.信号：转折 But + 对比 Instead of 。答案句的信号是双重的：先有转折 But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another，把"假期"的真实…

optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：C 的 He had a great time sightseeing and relaxing. 偷了录音里的原词 relaxing 来勾你选，可原文是 Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot——relaxing 前面正挂着 Instead of（不是…而是），意思恰恰是"没在放松"。听到 relaxing 就选，正好掉进"原词被否定"的坑。 借用原文：No, very few relatively
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 的 He met many tourists from other countries. 听上去呼应开头那句 Not too many other tourists around, were there? 里的 tourists，但原文男士回答的是 No, very few relatively（游客很少），并未说"遇到很多别国游客"；这是借 tourists 一词做的答非所问。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 的 He managed to visit a different city each day. 描绘"每天去不同城市"，但男士全程只谈"换住处找最好的"（accommodation / best spot），从没提过"每天换城市"。它用"不停移动"的画面感来诱你联想，实属未提及。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（trying to find the perfect place ↔ looking for the best place to stay perfect=best，place 同指住处）

questions.evidenceText: But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another, trying to find the perfect place. Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot.

questions.stem: What does the woman say people tend to do when making decisions?

options.text: Prioritize what is essential to their best advantage.
Stretch out the process in search of the optimal.
Deliberate the consequences that may occur.
Take all relevant factors into consideration.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Essentially, we have this tendency to keep stretching out the decision-making process, because as human beings, we are hard-wired to optimize.信号：tendency to + 总结词 Essentially 。答案信号是"总结+点天性"：Essentially（本质上）领出结论，紧跟 we have this tendency to keep stretchin…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：A 的 Prioritize what is essential to their best advantage. 用 best advantage 蹭整段反复出现的 best/optimize 之感，但原文说的是"人会拖长过程"，不是"优先抓要紧事"；prioritize（优先排序）这层意思原文从未提及，是借相近语感造的干扰。
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：C 的 Deliberate the consequences that may occur.（仔细考虑可能的后果）听着也像"决策时的做法"，但原文 hard-wired to optimize 讲的是"追求最优"，根本没提"权衡后果"，consequences 是凭空添的概念。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 的 Take all relevant factors into consideration. 是个放哪都对的万能说法，但原文女士说的是"人倾向拖长过程"，并未说"人会把所有相关因素都纳入考虑"；它靠"听起来很对"诱选，实为未提及。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（keep stretching out the decision-making process ↔ Stretch out the process 近乎同形，只略作删减）

questions.evidenceText: Essentially, we have this tendency to keep stretching out the decision-making process, because as human beings, we are hard-wired to optimize.

questions.stem: What has made decision making increasingly difficult?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：But I think thanks to technology, we can make comparisons more easily and have more access to choice and customization. We keep looking over and return to the same options again and again.信号：因果信号 thanks to 。答案信号是因果短语 thanks to technology——thanks to（多亏、由于）直接引出原因 technology，其后 we can make comparisons…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：A 的 Time pressure. 是"做事难"时最顺常识的猜想，但录音从头到尾没把"时间压力"列为决策变难的原因，反倒第 7 段女士主张"要投入时间去研究"；Time pressure 纯属凭常识脑补，未提及。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 的 Tight budget. 把成因引向"钱不够"，但全程谈的是"选择太多、反复纠结"，从没提过预算或花钱，属凭空添加的原因，未提及。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 的 Fierce competition. 同属"现代社会通病"类词、听感和 Modern technology 一样"像那么回事"，但录音从未把 competition 当成决策变难的原因，是借相近气质设的干扰，未提及。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（thanks to technology ↔ Modern technology technology 加修饰 Modern，同指一物）

questions.evidenceText: But I think thanks to technology, we can make comparisons more easily and have more access to choice and customization. We keep looking over and return to the same options again and again.

questions.stem: According to the woman, what should people do when making important decisions?

options.text: Research as many different options as possible.
Avoid going over the same options repeatedly.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P7）：What you need to do is research: have a process, invest time exploring your options, and eliminate as many things as you can. The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again.信号：建议句 What you need to do + 最高级 most toxic 。答案信号有两处：What you need to do is research 是直接的建议句（你需要做的是…），亮出女士的主张；而…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 的 Research as many different options as possible. 偷用了原文 What you need to do is research 的 research 来诱选，但女士的 research 强调的是"有流程、投入时间、并 eliminate 排除掉尽量多的选项"，而非 as many…as possible（尽可能多地研究选项）；A 把"排除"说反成"尽量多留"，且没体现题问的"重要决定"落点，属盗原词的答非所问。 借用原文：trusting your gut is not practical
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 的 Focus on what is practical. 用了原文出现的 practical，但原文是 When you have 30 odd options, trusting your gut is not practical——practical 是用来说"凭直觉不实际"的，并非建议"专注于实际的事"；选项截走 practical 一词另造主张，属原词被挪用。 借用原文：gut instinct might be overrated
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：D 的 Trust their gut instinct. 直接搬来原文的 gut，但女士明说 gut instinct might be overrated、trusting your gut is not practical——直觉被高估、不实际，是被否定的做法。听到 gut instinct 就选，正中"先抬后否"的陷阱。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again ↔ Avoid going over the same options repeatedly "最有害"=应避免，肯否定转换）

questions.evidenceText: What you need to do is research: have a process, invest time exploring your options, and eliminate as many things as you can. The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again.

transcript.text: The role of homework in classrooms is not a new debate. Many parents and teachers are ardent supporters of homework. But do all students benefit from homework? A 2006 research paper suggested some correlation between the amount of homework done by a student and future academic achievement for middle and high school students but not so much for younger kids.
transcript.zh: 家庭作业在课堂教学中的作用并不是一个新争论。许多家长和教师都是家庭作业的热烈支持者。但所有学生都能从家庭作业中受益吗？2006年的一篇研究论文指出，对于初中和高中生而言，学生完成的作业量与未来的学业成就之间存在一定的相关性，但对于年龄更小的孩子来说则不然。

transcript.text: A Stanford study in 2014 suggested the same was true for students in California's affluent communities. The findings challenged the idea that homework was "inherently good." The researchers concluded that there was an upper limit to the correlation between homework and achievement, suggesting that high school students shouldn't be doing more than two hours of homework a night. And the most valuable kind of homework for elementary-level children was simply assigned free reading.
transcript.zh: 2014年斯坦福大学的一项研究表明，加利福尼亚州富裕社区的学生也是如此。研究结果挑战了家庭作业“本质上是有益的”这一观念。研究人员得出结论，家庭作业与学业成就之间的相关性存在上限，并建议高中生每晚做家庭作业的时间不应超过两小时。而对于小学阶段的孩子来说，最有价值的家庭作业仅仅是布置的自由阅读。

transcript.text: The topic gets more complicated when we talk about the divide between rural and urban communities. Studies found that in remote areas, the poor quality or lack of internet access can put students at a disadvantage because 70% of teachers in these areas assign homework that requires internet access. But one in three households doesn't have internet. Experts assert homework requiring the internet isn't fair.
transcript.zh: 当我们谈到城乡社区之间的差距时，这个话题变得更加复杂。研究发现，在偏远地区，网络质量差或缺乏网络连接会使学生处于不利地位，因为这些地区70%的教师布置的家庭作业都需要使用网络。但三分之一的家庭没有网络。专家断言，需要使用网络的家庭作业是不公平的。

transcript.text: While the debate continues about the effect of homework on academic achievements, there are studies focusing on other benefits of homework. A study in Germany found that homework could have an effect on students' personalities, suggesting that doing homework might help kids to become more conscientious and independent learners.
transcript.zh: 尽管关于家庭作业对学业成就影响的争论仍在继续，但也有研究关注家庭作业的其他益处。德国的一项研究发现，家庭作业可能会对学生的性格产生影响，这表明做家庭作业可能有助于孩子们成为更认真尽责、更独立的学习者。

questions.stem: What did the 2006 research find about homework?

options.text: It is beneficial to poor as well as rich communities.
It is conducive to children's future development.
It is welcome to parents but not to children.
It is not of much help to younger children.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A 2006 research paper suggested some correlation between the amount of homework done by a student and future academic achievement for middle and high school students but not so much for younger kids.信号：转折 but 之后才是落点 。本句靠转折信号 but not so much for younger kids 定位：but 之前讲初高中生有关联是铺垫，but 之后对低龄孩子的"没那么有用"才是该研究真正要强调的发…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：poor as well as rich communities 里的 communities 是录音第 2 段 affluent communities 才出现的词，与 2006 研究无关；本题问的是 2006 研究，A 把别处的词搬来凑，且"贫富通吃"在原文也无依据。 借用原文：future academic achievement for middle and high school students
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：conducive to children's future development 借用了答案句前半 future academic achievement 的 future 一词，但那半句讲的是初高中生才有关联、是被 but 推翻的铺垫，B 误把铺垫当成总结论且笼统说成对所有 children 有益，与原文按年龄分层的发现不符。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：welcome to parents but not to children 谈的是家长欢迎、孩子不欢迎的态度，录音第 1 段只提到 Many parents and teachers are ardent supporters，从没说孩子的好恶，更没说 2006 研究有此发现，属凭空添加。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（not so much for younger kids ↔ not of much help to younger children not so much 同义改写为 not of much help）

questions.evidenceText: A 2006 research paper suggested some correlation between the amount of homework done by a student and future academic achievement for middle and high school students but not so much for younger kids.

questions.stem: What do experts think of homework requiring internet access?

options.text: It may put some students in remote areas at a disadvantage.
It gives the majority of students ready access to their teachers.
It effectively improves the learning quality of students in rural areas.
It can bridge the learning gap between kids of different backgrounds.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P3）：Studies found that in remote areas, the poor quality or lack of internet access can put students at a disadvantage because 70% of teachers in these areas assign homework that requires internet access.... Experts assert homework requiring the internet isn't fair.信号：专家断言句 + isn't fair 评价词 。定位靠两处信号：一是 Experts assert 直接对应题干问的"专家看法"，二是评价词 put students at a disadvantage 与 isn'…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：ready access to their teachers 借了录音反复出现的 access 一词（internet access），却换成"多数学生能便捷接触老师"，原文谈的是网络接入而非接触老师，且强调的是大量人没有网络，B 既偷换概念又把困难说成便利。 借用原文：can put students at a disadvantage
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：improves the learning quality of students in rural areas 借用 remote areas 同义的 rural areas 谈农村学生，却说"提升学习质量"，与专家 isn't fair、at a disadvantage 的负面定性完全相反，是典型的正话反说。 借用原文：put students at a disadvantage
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：bridge the learning gap between kids of different backgrounds 听起来很正面，但原文讲的是联网作业反而让缺网的偏远学生更吃亏、加大而非弥合差距，方向相反，且"弥合差距"原文从未表达。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（can put students at a disadvantage ↔ put some students in remote areas at a disadvantage 几乎同形的劣势表述对应）

questions.evidenceText: Studies found that in remote areas, the poor quality or lack of internet access can put students at a disadvantage because 70% of teachers in these areas assign homework that requires internet access.... Experts assert homework requiring the internet isn't fair.

questions.stem: What conclusion could be drawn from the study in Germany?

options.text: Diligent students tend to do their homework independently.
The focus of homework should always be on school subjects.
Doing homework exerts a positive effect on kids' personality development.
The benefits of doing homework vary widely from individual to individual.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：A study in Germany found that homework could have an effect on students' personalities, suggesting that doing homework might help kids to become more conscientious and independent learners.信号：研究标志词 in Germany + suggesting 引出结论 。定位靠 A study in Germany found that 对应题干所问研究，再靠 suggesting that 引出该研究的结论；结…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Diligent students tend to do their homework independently. 借了录音的 independent 一词，但原文说的是"做作业使孩子变独立"，A 反过来说"勤奋学生倾向独立做作业"，把因果方向掉了头，原文并无此说。 借用原文：not so much for younger kids
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：The focus of homework should always be on school subjects. 含绝对词 always，谈的是作业内容该聚焦学科，而德国研究讲的是作业对性格的影响，根本没讨论作业内容该放在哪，属未提及加绝对化。
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：The benefits of doing homework vary widely from individual to individual. 听起来稳妥，但德国研究的结论是统一指向"影响性格"，并未说作业益处因人而异；"因个体差异"更接近第 1、2 段按年龄/社区分层的内容，被错安到德国研究头上。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（an effect on students' personalities ↔ exerts a positive effect on kids' personality development have an effect=exerts an effect，personalities=personality）

questions.evidenceText: A study in Germany found that homework could have an effect on students' personalities, suggesting that doing homework might help kids to become more conscientious and independent learners.

transcript.text: Robert Goddard, an American born in 1882, is widely regarded as the world's first rocket scientist.
transcript.zh: 罗伯特·戈达德是一位1882年出生的美国人，被广泛认为是世界上第一位火箭科学家。

transcript.text: At age 27, Goddard published his first book in which he hypothesized that a rocket launched from Earth could reach the Moon. Like many visionaries, the young scientist encountered numerous skeptics. In January 1920, The New York Times ridiculed Goddard's theory that rockets could be utilized for space exploration. Forty-nine years later, Apollo 11 reached the Moon and the famed newspaper published an apology to Goddard.
transcript.zh: 27岁时，戈达德出版了他的第一本书，在书中提出了从地球发射的火箭可以抵达月球的假说。像许多有远见的人一样，这位年轻的科学家遇到了众多质疑者。1920年1月，《纽约时报》嘲笑了戈达德关于火箭可以用于太空探索的理论。49年后，阿波罗11号抵达月球，这家著名报纸发表了一篇向戈达德道歉的文章。

transcript.text: Goddard launched his first rocket from an aunt's farm in his native Massachusetts in March, 1926. His maiden rocket voyage lasted a mere 3 seconds. It scaled an altitude of only 12 meters. Nonetheless, it was a milestone in rocket science.
transcript.zh: 1926年3月，戈达德从家乡马萨诸塞州一位姨母的农场发射了他的第一枚火箭。这枚火箭的首次飞行仅持续了3秒。它达到的高度只有12米。尽管如此，这仍是火箭科学领域的一个里程碑。

transcript.text: Goddard later consulted with a weather expert and determined that the climate of New Mexico was ideal for year-round rocket launches. In 1930, Goddard and his family relocated there, to a remote valley in the southwest of the country. There he established a laboratory and test range.
transcript.zh: 后来，戈达德向一位气象专家进行了咨询，并确定新墨西哥州的气候非常适合全年发射火箭。1930年，戈达德和家人搬到了那里，定居在美国西南部一个偏远的山谷中。他在那里建立了一个实验室和试验场。

transcript.text: However, the ambitious scientist received negligible support from the government. For four years, wealthy businessman Daniel Guggenheim provided Goddard with an annual 25,000 dollars grant to pursue his dreams. Other rocket enthusiasts also raised funds for him. Over time, Goddard's rocket grew more sophisticated and included the installation of instruments.
transcript.zh: 然而，这位雄心勃勃的科学家几乎没有得到政府的支持。四年来，富有的商人丹尼尔·古根海姆每年向戈达德提供2.5万美元的资助，以支持他追逐梦想。其他火箭爱好者也为他筹集资金。随着时间的推移，戈达德的火箭变得越来越复杂，并增设了各种仪器。

transcript.text: In spite of his many successes, Goddard was never able to interest the US military in rocket-propelled weapons. He was granted over 200 patents and continued to pioneer rocket technology until his death in 1945.
transcript.zh: 尽管取得了许多成功，戈达德始终未能使美国军方对火箭推进武器产生兴趣。他获得了200多项专利，并一直致力于开创火箭技术，直到1945年去世。

questions.stem: What do we learn about Goddard's idea of using rockets for space exploration?

options.text: It was something he apologized for later.
It was ridiculed by the New York Times.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：In January 1920, The New York Times ridiculed Goddard's theory that rockets could be utilized for space exploration.信号：专有名词+负面动词定位 。答案句的信号是专有名词 The New York Times 加一个鲜明的负面动词 ridiculed（嘲笑）。听到《纽约时报》这个被原样念出的机构名，再抓住紧跟的那个评价动词 ridicu…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：录音里道歉的是《纽约时报》后来 published an apology to Goddard（向戈达德道歉），而 It was something he apologized for later 说成是戈达德自己为这设想道歉，主体被调换，正话说反。 借用原文：Forty-nine years later, Apollo 11 reached the Moon
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音说 Forty-nine years later, Apollo 11 reached the Moon——49年指的是从被嘲笑到登月之间隔的年数，而 It was a forty-nine-year plan 硬把 49 说成一个49年的计划，盗用数字 49 却扭曲了它的含义。 借用原文：Like many visionaries, the young scientist encountered numerous skeptics
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音说 Like many visionaries（像许多有远见者一样），visionary 是形容戈达德这类人，且紧接着讲他遭遇质疑者；It was considered visionary 把 visionary 安到这个设想头上、说它当年被视为有远见，与录音随后描述的被嘲笑境遇相反。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（The New York Times ridiculed Goddard's theory ↔ It was ridiculed by the New York Times 主动改被动、对象不变）

questions.evidenceText: In January 1920, The New York Times ridiculed Goddard's theory that rockets could be utilized for space exploration.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Goddard's first rocket voyage?

options.text: It was of great significance to rocket science.
It was completed in the state of New Mexico.
It was somehow delayed about 12 minutes.
It failed due to a sudden change of weather.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：His maiden rocket voyage lasted a mere 3 seconds. It scaled an altitude of only 12 meters. Nonetheless, it was a milestone in rocket science.信号：转折 Nonetheless 后才是定性 。前两句净说短处（a mere 3 seconds、only 12 meters），真正给这次首飞定性的，是转折词 Nonetheless 之后那句——milestone（里…

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：录音明说首飞在 his native Massachusetts（家乡马萨诸塞），而 completed in the state of New Mexico 把地点换成新墨西哥——新墨西哥是他后来搬去的地方（第4段），与首飞不是一回事，地点张冠李戴。 借用原文：It scaled an altitude of only 12 meters
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音里 12 来自 an altitude of only 12 meters（高度仅12米），delayed about 12 minutes 盗用数字 12，却把它从米偷换成延迟的分钟，单位和含义全变了。 借用原文：Nonetheless, it was a milestone in rocket science
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：录音对首飞的定性是 it was a milestone（里程碑，成功），并未说失败，全段也没提天气；failed due to a sudden change of weather 既反了结果、又凭空加了天气原因。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（it was a milestone in rocket science ↔ It was of great significance to rocket science 里程碑=意义重大的同义替换）

questions.evidenceText: His maiden rocket voyage lasted a mere 3 seconds. It scaled an altitude of only 12 meters. Nonetheless, it was a milestone in rocket science.

questions.stem: Why did Goddard move to New Mexico?

options.text: A laboratory and test range was already set up there.
Its climate was ideal for year-round rocket launching.
A weather expert invited him to go there for his mission.
Its remote valleys were appealing to him and his family.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：Goddard later consulted with a weather expert and determined that the climate of New Mexico was ideal for year-round rocket launches.信号：determined that 引出判断即原因 。答案信号是 determined that the climate…was ideal for year-round rocket launches——determi…

optionAnalysis.A: 答非所问：录音里 There he established a laboratory and test range（在那儿他建立了实验室和试验场）发生在搬过去之后，是结果不是原因；A laboratory and test range was already set up there 还加了 already（早已建好），与原文先搬后建的顺序相反。 借用原文：Goddard later consulted with a weather expert
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：录音是 consulted with a weather expert（他咨询了气象专家）以获取气候判断，而 A weather expert invited him to go there 把气象专家说成是邀请他去的人，凭空捏造了邀请这一动作。 借用原文：Goddard and his family relocated there, to a remote valley in the southwest of the country
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音说他搬 to a remote valley in the southwest（搬到西南部一处偏僻山谷），remote valley 只是描述落脚地，并未说山谷吸引了他全家；Its remote valleys were appealing to him and his family 把地点描述硬说成搬家的吸引原因，且 appealing 系原文所无。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the climate of New Mexico was ideal for year-round rocket launches ↔ Its climate was ideal for year-round rocket launching 近乎原句的轻微改写）

questions.evidenceText: Goddard later consulted with a weather expert and determined that the climate of New Mexico was ideal for year-round rocket launches.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Goddard's achievements?

options.text: He won an award from the US government for his work.
He gained recognition from rocket scientists worldwide.
He was granted over 200 patents in rocket technology.
He boosted the military strength of the United States.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：He was granted over 200 patents and continued to pioneer rocket technology until his death in 1945.信号：被原样念出的数字硬指标 。答案句的信号是一个被原样念出的可量化硬指标 granted over 200 patents（被授予200多项专利）。成就题里，这种数字+专有概念的句子最实、最难造假，听到 over 200…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：录音说 received negligible support from the government（几乎没得到政府支持），与得奖恰相反；He won an award from the US government 盗用 government 一词，却把没获政府支持反说成获政府颁奖。 借用原文：Goddard was never able to interest the US military in rocket-propelled weapons
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：录音只提资助他的富商和其他火箭爱好者（Other rocket enthusiasts also raised funds for him），从未说他获得全球火箭科学家的认可；gained recognition from rocket scientists worldwide 是原文未提及的内容。
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：录音说 was never able to interest the US military in rocket-propelled weapons（始终未能让美国军方对火箭动力武器感兴趣），与增强军力相反；He boosted the military strength 盗用 military，却把军方不感兴趣反说成他增强了军力。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（He was granted over 200 patents ↔ He was granted over 200 patents in rocket technology 近原句、补限定语）

questions.evidenceText: He was granted over 200 patents and continued to pioneer rocket technology until his death in 1945.

transcript.text: Working for a new venture comes with a lot of risks. There's instability, unclear responsibilities, and the need to be a master of all trades. But the primary benefit is usually the passion and excitement associated with playing a role in a promising new company. The person to thank for that passion and excitement is almost always the entrepreneur.
transcript.zh: 为一家新创企业工作伴随着诸多风险。企业可能缺乏稳定性，职责也不明确，而且需要一个人样样都能胜任。但其主要益处通常在于，能够参与一家前景可观的新公司，并从中获得激情与兴奋感。几乎总是应该感谢企业家的，正是这种激情与兴奋感。

transcript.text: There's something about the founder's energy and enthusiasm that infects the rest of the team. The willingness to take risks may inspire others to be more courageous. The optimism and positivity may motivate people to focus less on trivial and unimportant matters. The celebration of milestones may prompt staff to be more grateful about their own accomplishments and privileges.
transcript.zh: 创始人的活力与热情总有一种感染团队其他成员的力量。敢于承担风险的意愿可能会激励他人变得更加勇敢。乐观积极的态度可能促使人们少关注琐碎且无关紧要的事情。对里程碑的庆祝可能会促使员工更加感激自己的成就与所拥有的优势。

transcript.text: What becomes set in the firm's culture is a contagious collection of affirmative and positive emotions which are usually shared among the team. Science has already done a good job of proving the results that follow. These include better processes, greater team cohesion, reduced conflict and sharper alertness.
transcript.zh: 最终融入公司文化的，是一系列具有传染性的肯定且积极的情绪，而这些情绪通常会在团队成员之间共享。科学研究已经很好地证明了随之而来的结果，其中包括更完善的流程、更强的团队凝聚力、更少的冲突以及更加敏锐的警觉性。

transcript.text: But what is yet to be demonstrated is whether the founder's passion leads to increased team performance. This was recently tested in research, which analyzed the teams of 73 new companies across a range of industries such as IT, medicine and energy. The CEOs were consulted once again, years after the initial analysis. And most shared their firm's performance reports, so that their success could be more objectively measured.
transcript.zh: 但创始人的激情是否会带来团队绩效的提升，尚未得到证明。最近，一项研究对此进行了检验，分析了73家新公司的团队，这些公司涵盖IT、医疗和能源等多个行业。研究人员在初次分析数年后再次向这些公司的首席执行官进行了咨询。大多数首席执行官都提供了公司的绩效报告，从而使研究人员能够更加客观地衡量其成功程度。

transcript.text: Entrepreneurial teams generally progress through three phases. The first is inventing a product or service, the second is founding the venture to sell that product or service, and the third is developing the firm so it continues to grow.
transcript.zh: 创业团队通常会经历三个阶段。第一阶段是发明一种产品或服务，第二阶段是创办企业来销售该产品或服务，第三阶段则是发展公司，使其能够持续增长。

transcript.text: The researchers discovered that when the team is passionate about the third phase—developing the firm—there's a clear link to performance. But the first phase—a passion for invention—is not a reliable indicator that the firm will still be open for business a few years later. Likewise, the second—a passion for founding the venture—doesn't necessarily translate into great success.
transcript.zh: 研究人员发现，当团队对第三阶段，也就是发展公司，充满热情时，这与绩效之间存在明确的联系。但第一阶段，即对发明的热情，并不能可靠地表明这家公司几年后仍会继续营业。同样，第二阶段，即对创办企业的热情，也未必能转化为巨大的成功。

transcript.text: The solution to great team performance stems from a willingness to recruit others who could direct their passion towards the third phase of entrepreneurialism: developing the business. Employing more staff can in itself be a risk for an entrepreneur, as is paying them big dollars to attract them. On many occasions, the entrepreneurs reported not paying themselves a wage at all initially, in order to cover salaries and expenses.

transcript.text: Ageing is a curious thing and people's desire to beat it—and death—has become an industry worth hundreds of billions of dollars.
transcript.zh: 衰老是一件奇妙的事情，而人们想要战胜衰老乃至死亡的愿望，已经催生了一个价值数千亿美元的产业。

transcript.text: Despite the huge investment into research, ageing remains somewhat obscure, although there are certain things researchers do understand. They know that women tend to have longer lifespans, living on average six years longer than men. No one is really certain of the reason for this, although the speculation centers around the idea that women are more capable of surviving or handling disease than men. For virtually every disease, the effects are greater on men than they are on women.
transcript.zh: 尽管投入了巨资进行研究，衰老仍然在一定程度上鲜为人知，不过研究人员确实了解一些情况。他们知道，女性往往寿命更长，平均比男性多活六年。没有人真正确定其中的原因，不过有人推测，这可能是因为女性比男性更有能力挺过疾病或应对疾病。几乎对于每一种疾病，男性受到的影响都比女性更大。

transcript.text: Some suggest that women's immune systems benefit from their tendency to prioritize and nurture social connections. But for me, this explanation is hardly convincing.
transcript.zh: 有人认为，女性倾向于优先维系和培养社会关系，这使她们的免疫系统受益。但对我而言，这种解释很难令人信服。

transcript.text: Researchers also know, to an extent, what causes ageing. For 60 years, it was believed that cells would continue to divide forever. It was only uncovered in relatively recent times that older people's cells divide a smaller number of times than younger people's. Only cancer cells, in fact, are capable of dividing forever. Human cells have a limited reproductive ability. To an extent, we can postpone the eventual stop of cells' dividing, through nutrition, exercise, good sleep, and even relaxation techniques. But we cannot stop the ageing process.
transcript.zh: 研究人员也在一定程度上了解衰老的原因。在长达60年的时间里，人们一直认为细胞会不断分裂下去，永远不会停止。直到相对较近的时期，人们才发现，老年人的细胞分裂次数少于年轻人的。事实上，只有癌细胞能够无限分裂。人体细胞的繁殖能力是有限的。在一定程度上，我们可以通过营养、锻炼、良好的睡眠，甚至放松技巧，推迟细胞最终停止分裂的时间。但我们无法阻止衰老过程。

transcript.text: And researchers are yet to answer the ultimate question of ageing. Why does the body ultimately fall to pieces?
transcript.zh: 而研究人员尚未回答有关衰老的终极问题：身体最终为什么会衰败？

transcript.text: In the opinion of some of the world's best scientific minds on the subject, part of the reason we don't yet have an answer is because many researchers are looking in the wrong direction. Many public health policy makers believe that the resolution of age-associated disease will tell us something fundamental about the ageing process, but say some top scientists, that's completely erroneous. They point to when the diseases of childhood were eliminated, but this did not provide any insight into childhood development. In the same way, the idea that the resolution of age-associated disease like heart disease and stroke will inform us about ageing is not based on sound science or logic.
transcript.zh: 在该领域一些世界顶尖科学家的看法中，我们至今尚未找到答案，部分原因在于许多研究人员的研究方向错了。许多公共卫生政策制定者认为，解决与年龄相关的疾病将使我们了解衰老过程中的某些根本问题，但一些顶尖科学家说，这种看法完全错误。他们指出，儿童期疾病被消除之后，并没有因此让人们对儿童成长发育有任何深入了解。同样，认为解决心脏病和中风等与年龄相关的疾病就能让我们了解衰老，这一想法没有坚实的科学或逻辑依据。

transcript.text: At best, if the major causes of death in developed countries were eliminated, this would only add a decade to average life expectancy. But while there is money available to be spent on it, the search to understand the secrets of ageing will be ongoing.
transcript.zh: 充其量，即使发达国家消除了导致死亡的主要原因，也只能使平均预期寿命增加十年。不过，只要还有资金可以投入，对衰老奥秘的探索就将持续下去。

transcript.text: Good afternoon. In today's talk, we'll discuss how managers can get their staff to do what they are asked.
transcript.zh: 下午好。今天的讲座中，我们将讨论管理者如何让员工按照要求完成工作。

transcript.text: Much to their frustration, managers often struggle to get their staff to comply with even simple instructions. Often they blame their employees: "They don't read emails, they don't listen, they don't care"-that kind of thing. But according to recent research conducted in Australia, it looks like it's not the employees' fault but the managers'.
transcript.zh: 令管理者深感沮丧的是，他们常常难以让员工遵守哪怕是简单的指示。他们往往把责任归咎于员工：“他们不读邮件，不听指示，也不在乎——诸如此类。”但根据澳大利亚近期开展的一项研究，问题似乎不在员工，而在管理者。

transcript.text: It's easy to understand why people sometimes disobey procedures intentionally. Occasionally, it's because they're pressured to finish in a short time. At other times, they may disagree with the spirit of the procedure, the effort demanded, the time consumed, the lack of potential effectiveness. And every now and then, they just don't want to, maybe deliberately or out of stubbornness.
transcript.zh: 人们有时会故意不遵守程序，这一点很容易理解。有时是因为他们受到压力，必须在很短的时间内完成工作。另一些时候，他们可能不同意程序的宗旨，或认为程序要求付出的努力太多、耗费的时间太长，或者潜在的成效不足。还有些时候，他们只是不想遵守，可能是故意如此，也可能是出于固执。

transcript.text: So apart from that, what else gets in the way of procedural compliance? The research scholars surveyed 152 blue-collar workers from two separate sites in the mining industry. They asked the workers a range of procedure-related questions, such as whether they found the procedures useful, how confident they felt in their job, how comfortable they were to speak up in the workplace, and how closely they followed any new procedures set by their managers. They were also asked to rate the extent to which they perceived their supervisors to be helpful.
transcript.zh: 那么，除此之外，还有什么因素会妨碍人们遵守程序呢？研究人员对采矿业两个不同工作地点的152名蓝领工人进行了调查。他们向工人提出了一系列与程序有关的问题，例如他们是否认为这些程序有用、对自己的工作有多大信心、在工作场所发言时是否感到自在，以及他们在多大程度上遵循管理者制定的任何新程序。他们还被要求评价自己认为主管在多大程度上能够提供帮助。

transcript.text: That last statement was the most instructive because, as the researchers found, there was a remarkably strong correlation between how helpful supervisors were perceived to be and how likely their employees were to follow their directives. Supervisors' helping behavior was found to be motivational in nature. It increased employees' perception of the likelihood of success in the attainment of job goals, and therefore fostered a willingness to dedicate their effort and ability to their work.
transcript.zh: 最后一点最能说明问题，因为研究人员发现，人们认为主管是否乐于提供帮助，与员工是否愿意遵循主管的指示之间存在显著的强相关性。研究发现，主管的帮助行为具有激励作用。这种行为提高了员工对实现工作目标成功可能性的认识，因此促使他们愿意将自己的努力和能力投入工作。

transcript.text: In short, managers should be ongoing role models for the change. As the saying goes: "Do as I do, not as I say". To affect behavioral change, what's most required is interaction and involvement—the human touch—and, naturally, processes that add value. Although procedures are designed to guide and support employees' work, employees, it seems, can't always be expected to comply with procedures that are not seen as useful. And of course, managers shouldn't keep resending emails. They're an effective tool for the sharing of data and reports, but they're a hopeless tool if what a manager is desiring is a change in behavior.
transcript.zh: 简而言之，管理者应当持续以身作则，推动变革。正如俗话所说：“照我做，而不是照我说的做。”要促进行为改变，最需要的是互动和参与——人与人之间的沟通——当然还需要能够创造价值的流程。虽然程序旨在指导和支持员工的工作，但看来，我们不能总是期待员工遵守那些被认为没有用处的程序。当然，管理者也不应一遍遍地重新发送邮件。邮件是分享数据和报告的有效工具，但如果管理者想要改变员工的行为，邮件就完全不起作用了。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Notre Dame Cathedral in the heart of Paris was within "15 to 30 minutes" of complete destruction as firefighters battled to stop flames reaching its bell towers on Monday evening, French authorities have revealed. A greater disaster was averted by members of the Paris fire brigade, who risked their lives to remain inside the burning monument to create a wall of water between the raging fire and the two towers on the west of the building.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The revelation of how close France came to losing its most famous cathedral emerged as police investigators questioned workers involved in the restoration of the monument to try to establish the cause of the devastating blaze. Paris prosecutor Remy Heitz said that an initial fire alert was sounded at 6:20 pm on Monday evening but no fire was found. The second alert was sounded at 6:43 pm, and the blaze was discovered on the roof.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: More than €650 million was raised in a few hours on Tuesday as French business leaders and global corporations announced they would donate to a restoration campaign launched by the president, Emmanuel Macron. But as the emergency services picked through the burnt debris, a row was resurfacing over accusations that the beloved cathedral, immortalised in Victor Hugo's novel, was already crumbling before the fire.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The cathedral is owned by the French state and has been at the centre of a years-long dispute over who should finance restoration work of the collapsing staircases, crumbling statues and cracked walls. Jean-Michel Leniaud, the president of the scientific council at the National Heritage Institute, said: "What happened was bound to happen. The lack of adequate maintenance and daily attention to such a majestic building is the cause of this catastrophe." After the blaze was declared completely extinguished, 15 hours after it started, the junior interior minister, Laurent Nunez, said the structure had been saved but remained vulnerable. He praised the actions of the firefighters but admitted the fate of the cathedral had been uncertain. "They saved the main structure, but it all came down to 15-30 minutes," Nunez said.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: In a surprise televised address on Tuesday evening, Macron said he wanted to see the cathedral rebuilt within five years. "The fire at Notre Dame reminds us that we will always have challenges to overcome," Macron said, "Notre Dame is our history, our literature, the centre of our life. It is the standard by which we measure our distances. It's so many books, so many paintings. It's the cathedral of every French person, even those who have never visited it. This history is ours and so we will rebuild Notre Dame. It is what the French people expect; it is what our history deserves. It is our deep destiny. We will rebuild Notre Dame so it is even more beautiful than before. I want it done in the next five years. We can do it. After the time of testing comes a time of reflection and then of action."

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The fire, which had started at the base of the 93-metre spire(尖塔) at about 6:40 pm on Monday, spread through the cathedral's roof, made up of hundreds of oak beams, some dating back to the 13th century. These beams, known as la forêt (the forest) because of their density, formed the cross-shaped roof that ran the length of the central part of the cathedral. As hundreds of tourists and Parisians stood and watched the flames leaping from the roof, there was shock and tears as the cathedral spire caught fire, burned and then collapsed into itself.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: A collection of dramatic videos and photos quickly spread across social media, showing the horrifying destruction, and attracting emotional responses from people all over the world. Indeed, within minutes the fire occupied headlines of every major global newspaper and television network. This is not surprising given Notre Dame Cathedral, meaning "Our Lady", is one of the most recognised symbols of the city of Paris attracting millions of tourists every year.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: While the world looked on, the 500 firefighters at the scene then battled to prevent the flames from reaching the two main towers, where the cathedral bells hang. If the wooden frame of the towers had caught fire, it could have sent the bells—the largest of which, the Emmanuel Bell, weighs 13 tons—crashing down, potentially causing the collapse of both towers. Police and fire services will spend the next 48 hours assessing the "security and safety" of the 850-year-old structure. Nunez said: "We have identified vulnerabilities throughout the structure, all of which still need securing." As a result, residents of five buildings around the northern side of the cathedral were being temporarily evacuated, he added. Architects have identified three main holes in the structure, in the locations of the spire, the main hall and the upper rooms to the north of the central aisle. Most of the wooden roof beams have been burned, and parts of the concrete holding up the roof have collapsed.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: The interior minister, Christophe Castaner, visited the cathedral on Tuesday afternoon to see the extent of the devastation. Ash covered the marble diamond-patterned floor and floated in large pools of grey water from the fire hoses. Behind a heap of blackened oak beams that lay piled up where they had fallen, daylight from vast holes in the cathedral roof lit a golden cross over a statue by Nicolas Coustou, which appeared to have escaped damage. Preliminary inspections also suggested the three ornate(装饰华丽的) stained glass "rose" windows appeared to have survived the fire, officials said. However, fire officers have said a complete inventory of the damage will not be possible until the cathedral structure has been deemed safe.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: The culture minister, Franck Riester, said religious relics saved from the cathedral were being securely held at the Hotel de Ville, and works of art that sustained smoke damage were being taken to the Louvre, the world's largest art museum, where they would be dried out, repaired and stored. Sixteen copper statues that decorated the spire had been removed for restoration only a few days before the fire. Relics at the top of the spire are believed lost as the spire was destroyed. As well as damage from the heat, which firefighters said reached more than 800 ℃, experts also need to assess damage from the vast quantities of water firefighters poured into the cathedral. One casualty of this was The Great Organ constructed in the 1730s, which was said to have escaped the flames but been significantly damaged by water.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: French political commentators noted the devastating fire had succeeded where Macron had failed in uniting the country. But criticism over the original state of the building is likely to intensify over coming days. Leniaud told La Croix newspaper: "This is not about looking for people to blame. The responsibility is collective because this is the most loved monument in the country." Alexandre Gady, an art historian, agreed. "We've been saying for years that the budget for maintaining historic monuments is too low," Gady said. The Paris prosecutor's office has opened an inquiry into "involuntary destruction by fire", indicating they believe the cause of the blaze was accidental rather than criminal.

Dowd argues that we have misfiled the significance of drawing because we see it as a professional skill instead of a personal capacity. paragraphs.label: G

The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles but artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists. Cultivating drawing talent can become an essential tool to improve people's observational skills in fields where the visual is important.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Rather than think of drawing as a talent that some creative people are gifted in, we should consider it as a tool for seeing and understanding the world better—one that just so happens to double as an art form. Both absent-minded doodling and copying from life have been shown to positively affect your memory and visual perception, so complain loudly the next time your school board slashes the art department's budget.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The car has reshaped our cities. It seems to offer autonomy for everyone. There is something almost delightful in the detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom when most of their lives will be spent making short journeys on choked roads.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: For all the fuss made about top speeds, cornering ability and acceleration, the most useful gadgets on a modern car are those which work when you're going very slowly: parking sensors, sound systems, and navigation apps which will show a way around upcoming traffic jams. This seems to be one of the few areas where the benefit of sharing personal information comes straight back to the sharer: because these apps know where almost all the users are, and how fast they are moving almost all the time, they can spot traffic congestion(堵塞) very quickly and suggest ways round it.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The problem comes when everyone is using a navigation app which tells them to avoid everyone else using the same gadget. Traffic jams often appear where no one has enough information to avoid them. When a lucky few have access to the knowledge, they will benefit greatly. But when everyone has perfect information, traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: This new congestion teaches us two things. The first is that the promises of technology will never be realised as fully as we hope; they will be limited by their unforeseen and unintended consequences. Sitting in a more comfortable car in a different traffic jam is pleasant but hardly the liberation that once seemed to be promised. The second is that self-organisation will not get us where we want to go. The efforts of millions of drivers to get ahead do not miraculously produce a situation in which everyone does better than before, but one in which almost everyone does rather worse. Central control and collective organisation can produce smoother and fairer outcomes, though even that much is never guaranteed.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Similar limits can be foreseen for the much greater advances promised by self-driving cars. Last week, one operated by the taxi company Uber struck and killed a woman pushing her bicycle across a wide road in Arizona. This was the first recorded death involving a car which was supposed to be fully autonomous. Experts have said that it suggests a "catastrophic failure" of technology.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Increasingly, even Silicon Valley has to acknowledge the costs of the intoxicating(令人陶醉的) hurry that characterises its culture. What traffic teaches us is that reckless and uncontrolled change is as likely to harm us as it is to benefit us, and that thoughtful regulation is necessary for a better future.
